title: fix(objectql): an uninstall refused because another package extends one of its objects answers 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT with the way out, not 500 INTERNAL_ERROR
body:
Fixes #23505

Clause-②: no

Dispatched by the `domain:spec` seat 4 PM (`sunhaolin`) to session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm`, branch `claude/issue-23505-extension-refusal-409`, claim comment 6172782630.

## What changed

`SchemaRegistry.assertPackageUninstallable` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) threw a bare `Error` with no `code` and no `status` when the package owns an object another package extends (ADR-0029). `deletePackage` step 3 rethrows it as is, so `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` fell through `resolveThrownHttpError` to its `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` fallback. The caller could change the state that blocked the uninstall, but the answer said the server failed.

The fix is at the producer. The refusal is now an unexported `PackageUninstallExtendedError`, in the registry's house shape (`code`, `status` and `httpStatus`, like `NamespaceConflictError` and `ObjectOwnershipConflictError`):

- **`code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `status: 409`.** No new code: this is the standard catalog member that the verb's sibling refusals already answer for environment state (`dropStorageRemainingRowsRefusal`, and the shared-object pre-flight in PR #23504).
- **The way out comes first**, because a 4xx message can be truncated. The diagnostic sentence the refusal always carried follows, and it now names every extended object (the first five, then a count of the rest), each with its extenders in registration order. Measured at the door:

  > Uninstall the package that extends an object of "com.owner" first (com.ext), then uninstall "com.owner" again: a package cannot be uninstalled while another package extends an object it owns (objectExtensions, ADR-0029). Cannot uninstall package "com.owner": object "alpha" is extended by com.ext.

- **Structured fields** for in-process callers: `packageId`, `extendedObjects`, `extenders`.

The decision itself is unchanged: a package is refused in the same cases as before, and before any mutation. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is not edited. Step 3 already rethrows the registry's error as is, so the door gets the status without touching steps 1–4, which PR #23504 holds.

## Every caller, measured

| Caller | How it meets the throw | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `deletePackage` step 3, then `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` (`errorFromThrown(e, 500)`) | rethrown as is | `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` becomes `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the prescription. Nothing changes in storage or the registry (pinned below). |
| The same door on a host with no persisted half (the door calls `registry.uninstallPackage(id)` itself; terminal `errorFromThrown`) | thrown through `uninstallPackage` | Also `500` to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. The package and its object stay registered. Measured with a one-off probe, deleted after reading. Not pinned. |
| The door's safety net after a persisted delete, and `deletePackage` step 6 | caught; `console.warn` with the message | Log text only. |
| `@objectstack/cloud-connection` install-local withdrawal | caught; reads `err.message` only | The `cleanups` outcome is unchanged; only the log text changes. |
| `MetadataFacade.unregisterPackage`, `ObjectQL.unregisterObject(name, packageId)` | propagate | No production caller in the tree (`git grep`). |
| `ObjectQL.removePackage` | `force: true` | Never asks. |

## Tests

Every reading below is at `fdc2dc05fc` (this branch after merging `origin/main` at `222293f60a`), except the full objectql run, which is noted.

- **`packages/runtime/src/package-uninstall-store-refusal.integration.test.ts`** (the existing pin). It runs on a real stack: `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`, `PackageServicePlugin`, the protocol and `HttpDispatcher`, booted twice over one SQLite file.
  - The extender case moves from `{ status: 500, code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR' }` to `{ status: 409, code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT' }`. It also asserts the opening of the prescription and the object's name.
  - Every "nothing changes" assertion is kept: stored rows, registry entry and disable record, in the same process and after a restart.
  - New **CONTROL** case: the extender is installed as a real package, so the first uninstall is refused `409`. Then `DELETE` of the extender through the same door, and the same uninstall answers `200` and stays gone after a restart.
  - Result: 5/5 pass.
- **`packages/objectql/src/registry-assert-package-uninstallable.test.ts`** pins:
  - the envelope;
  - the prescription first;
  - every object and extender named, in walk order;
  - the singular wording;
  - the five-then-count cap;
  - the same refusal through `unregisterObjectsByPackage` and `uninstallPackage`.
- **`packages/objectql/src/registry.test.ts`**: the order pin added for the refusal-pass ordering fix now reads the order off the structured refusal (first refusable object first, its extenders in registration order) instead of the old sentence.

| runtime pin + `package-uninstall-org-scope` | 2 / 11 pass |

| metadata-protocol `deletePackage` tests | 10 / 140 pass |
| objectql `vitest run --project local` (at `a9a88b1e34`; the merge changed no objectql source, only the two tests re-run above) | 415 / 8095 pass |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`, same for runtime | exit 0; test-typecheck debt held |

## Ablation (the producer's `code` and `status` renamed away)

The mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 time; blob `69df6079e5a7` to `7d89ea3120fa`). objectql was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight` found the planted marker in 4 dist files.

- **Re-pinned case: red on exactly the status and code assertion.** It expected `{ status: 409, code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT' }` and received `{ status: 500, code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR' }`, which is the pre-fix answer.
- **CONTROL: red on its precondition** (`expected 500 to be 409`).
- **Envelope test in `registry-assert-package-uninstallable.test.ts`: red.**
- **Restore.** The blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty. After an objectql rebuild, `--absent` found the marker in 0 of 14 dist files, and the pin passed 5/5 again.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` at `fdc2dc05fc`: 68 derived, 67 run with `exit 0`, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

- **NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.** It answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) because it reads every package's `dist/` and no full workspace build was run locally. CI runs it.
- **The families this change reads most directly:**
  - `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` is green. `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is a standard member, so no table row is owed.
  - `check:error-status-conformance` is green. Its deriver records `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`/409 from `class PackageUninstallExtendedError`; I measured this by calling `deriveRuntimeStatuses` on `registry.ts`, because the report shows only four sites per code.
  - `check-adr-0087-registration` reports "no declared-breaking changeset (1 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)".
  - `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset` are green.
- **Extra readings outside the derived set:** `check:error-code-provenance` and `check:error-code-casing`, both `exit 0`.

The changeset is `.changeset/23505-extension-refusal-409.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, with FROM, TO and Unchanged sections.

## Acceptance notes

- **Two comments now say `500` where the door answers `409`.** Both are outside this claim's file surface and change no behaviour:
  - In `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `deletePackage` step 3: "The HTTP door answers it through its `catch` around this verb: `500`, nothing changed." PR #23504 holds that block.
  - In `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, in the DELETE arm: "which the `catch` above answers — `500`, nothing changed."
  - Suggested wording for both: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, the refusal's own envelope, nothing changed. Carrier: none.
- **A test fixture keeps the old text.** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.package-delete-refusal.test.ts` builds its fake refusal with the old sentence. It pins pass-through identity, not the text, so it stays valid.
- **"Detach" is not offered as a way out.** No verb detaches an extension short of uninstalling the extending package, or installing a version without it (not measured), so the message names only the measured remedy.
- **The no-persisted-half door path** (second row of the table) moves `500` to `409` too. It was measured, not pinned.
